payload.task_text:
I need a comprehensive enrollment report for all courses in our Canvas LMS. Please pull the enrollment data for every course and break it down by role type.

Create an Excel file called Canvas_Enrollment_Report.xlsx with two sheets. The "Enrollment Data" sheet should have columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Students count, Teachers count, and Total_Enrolled being the sum of Students and Teachers. Sort by Course_Code alphabetically. "Students" counts enrollments of type StudentEnrollment only, and "Teachers" counts enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment only (do not include TaEnrollment or other types in either count). Include a header row on both sheets (the Enrollment Data sheet uses its column names as the header; the Summary sheet uses columns `Metric` and `Value`).

The "Summary" sheet with Metric and Value should have Total_Courses, Total_Students across all courses, Total_Teachers, Largest_Course code with most students, and Smallest_Course code with fewest students. Total_Students is the sum of each course's student count (a student enrolled in multiple courses is counted once per course, not de-duplicated across courses).

After creating the report, send an email to registrar@openuniversity.ac.uk with subject "Canvas Enrollment Overview Report" summarizing the total enrollment numbers. The email body must include the three headline totals each on its own labelled line, exactly as: Total_Students: <value>, Total_Courses: <value>, Total_Teachers: <value> (using the actual computed numbers).

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete this task directly; do not dispatch sub-agents. Resolve the task's accessible workspace directory from the harness and write Canvas_Enrollment_Report.xlsx there, never to a hard-coded /workspace path.

Call canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), validate unique course IDs/codes/names, then issue all per-course count calls in one native-parallel response: for each literal returned course ID call canvas_get_course_grades(page=1, per_page=1, type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and canvas_get_course_grades(page=1, per_page=1, type=["TeacherEnrollment"]). Use pagination.total_count for Students and Teachers and do not fetch enrollment rows. Freeze one canonical 22-row table {course_code, course_name, students, teachers, total_enrolled=students+teachers}. Sort by course_code, compute the five Summary values once, and use course_code ascending as the deterministic tie-break for equal student counts.

The main agent is the sole workbook writer. Create exactly Enrollment Data and Summary with the exact task headers and literal values; read A1:E<last row> and A1:B6 back from the resolved output path and verify complete course coverage, totals, extrema, and absence of extra sheets.

Run the exact Sent-mail lookup for recipient registrar@openuniversity.ac.uk and subject Canvas Enrollment Overview Report natively in parallel with the workbook branch once the canonical payload is frozen. Read every candidate to verify the recipient, send exactly once only if absent, and make the body contain the three required labelled lines exactly: Total_Students, Total_Courses, and Total_Teachers. Read the retained message back and reconcile it with the workbook before finishing.

nodes.text:
You are planning a task. Do NOT execute any writes — you only have read-only tools. Produce an ordered, actionable plan.

TASK DESCRIPTION (from the user):
1. Pull enrollment data for ALL courses in a Canvas LMS instance.
2. Create an Excel file named Canvas_Enrollment_Report.xlsx (in the accessible workspace directory) with two sheets:
   - Sheet "Enrollment Data": columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Students, Teachers, Total_Enrolled (= Students + Teachers). Sort rows by Course_Code alphabetically (A-Z). Include a header row using those column names. "Students" counts ONLY enrollments of type StudentEnrollment; "Teachers" counts ONLY enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment (exclude TaEnrollment and any other types from both counts).
   - Sheet "Summary": columns Metric and Value, with rows: Total_Courses, Total_Students (sum across all courses of each course's student count — a student in multiple courses is counted once per course, NOT de-duplicated), Total_Teachers (same summing logic), Largest_Course (course code with the most students), Smallest_Course (course code with the fewest students). Include a header row (Metric, Value).
3. Send an email to registrar@openuniversity.ac.uk with subject "Canvas Enrollment Overview Report", body must include exactly three labelled lines (each on its own line): "Total_Students: <value>", "Total_Courses: <value>", "Total_Teachers: <value>" using the computed numbers, plus whatever summary prose is desired.

CONTEXT YOU SHOULD DISCOVER (read-only):
- Canvas MCP tools available: canvas_health_check, canvas_list_courses, canvas_list_account_courses, canvas_get_course, canvas_get_course_grades (returns enrollments with type/role and supports pagination), canvas_list_course_users, canvas_list_account_users, canvas_get_account, canvas_list_sub_accounts.
- Determine the account/course structure: which accounts exist, how many courses, how to enumerate all courses (likely via canvas_list_courses or canvas_list_account_courses for an account_id, possibly including sub-accounts).
- Determine the best way to obtain per-course enrollments broken down by role type (StudentEnrollment vs TeacherEnrollment). Consider canvas_get_course_grades with type[] filter (StudentEnrollment, TeacherEnrollment) and pagination (per_page up to 100, follow pagination.has_more), or canvas_list_course_users. Note enrollment_state filters may matter (e.g., active vs invited).
- Note there is an Excel MCP (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, rename_worksheet, etc.) and an email MCP (send_email) available to the executor.
- Workspace: the Excel file should be created at the agent workspace directory (the executor knows its absolute path; it is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-enrollment-overview/workspace — verify what exists there if useful).

DELIVERABLE: A step-by-step plan with, for each subtask: (a) dispatch decision — `self` (main agent), `explore` (read-only investigation), or `coder` (executor); (b) dependency: independent/parallelizable or must wait for a specific prior subtask; (c) concrete tool calls to make and any gotchas (pagination, filtering, sorting, tie-breaking for Largest/Smallest course). Also specify a verification strategy (how to confirm the Excel file contents and the email send). Keep the plan concise and actionable.
Plan enrollment report task

You are a read-only exploration agent. Your job: collect per-course enrollment counts from the Canvas LMS using ONLY read-only Canvas MCP tools, and report back a structured summary. Do NOT write anything, do NOT create files, do NOT send emails.

The Canvas instance has exactly these 22 courses (id -> course_code -> course_name), already enumerated:

8 CCC-2014B "Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)"
9 DDD-2013J "Data-Driven Design (Fall 2013)"

12 DDD-2014B "Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)"
13 EEE-2013J "Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2013)"

22 GGG-2014B "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014)"

TASK:
For EACH of the 22 courses, call the Canvas MCP tool `canvas_get_course_grades` TWICE:
1. With course_id=<id>, type=["StudentEnrollment"] (and per_page=1) — read the `pagination.total_count` from the response; that is the STUDENTS count.
2. With course_id=<id>, type=["TeacherEnrollment"] (and per_page=1) — read the `pagination.total_count` from the response; that is the TEACHERS count.

Use the `total_count` field from pagination as the authoritative count (verified: it exactly equals the number of enrollments of that type). Do NOT page through records, do NOT filter by enrollment_state, and do NOT include TaEnrollment or any other role type.

If for any course the total_count is missing/zero while you suspect records exist, page with per_page=100 following pagination.has_more and count enrollments by their `type` field, and note that in your report.

DELIVERABLE — report back a concise table, one line per course:
course_id | course_code | course_name | Students | Teachers
plus the exact totals: sum of all Students, sum of all Teachers, and count of courses (should be 22). Also flag any course where Students != its known total_students field (I have total_students from the catalog; include it if the response provides it, but the StudentEnrollment count is the authoritative Students value).
